samples.summary: The guard's safety rests on an unenforced invariant ("app-issued redirects are `replace`"); a push-style redirect toward /login already exists in the tree
samples.evidence: The provider only exempts `replace` from the prompt (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-165). Every auth-relevant redirect today is a replace (`PrivateRoute.tsx:36`, `PublicRoute.tsx:24`, `file-detail.tsx:242`, `document-detail.tsx:863`, `docs-detail.tsx:342`, `notes-detail.tsx:369`, `slides-detail.tsx:947`, `board-detail.tsx:252`), so I could not build a live exploit. But nothing mechanically enforces it: `<Navigate>` defaults to a push, and `packages/frontend/src/app/templates/template-landing.tsx:101` already does `navigate(signInPath(id))` — a *push* to `/login` — for the unauthenticated-use path. If any session/authorization redirect is written (or moved onto a route) as a push while a guard is registered, an active guard can hold it back and a "Stay" swallows it permanently (the issuing effect does not re-run), leaving the user parked on a route whose auth state has already changed. The added tests assert the exemption for one hand-written `<Link replace>` only; no lint rule or test asserts the invariant repo-wide.
searchedFor: grep for eslint rules mentioning Navigate / no-restricted-syntax in packages/frontend eslint configs

samples.summary: 401 eviction stays indefinitely refusable and performs no client-side teardown: the cookie is cleared server-side while the tab keeps rendering authenticated data and holds its Yorkie session
samples.evidence: `fetchWithAuth` answers an unrecoverable 401 by calling `logout({redirect:false})` (auth.ts:185) — which POSTs /auth/logout and invalidates the session — and then `redirectTo('/login')` (auth.ts:190), a full-page navigation that the `beforeunload` guard registered by `SyncStatusChip` (sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103) lets the user cancel. The latch release added here (auth.ts:57-61) makes the redirect retryable, but each retry is equally refusable, so a user can keep an app open indefinitely after their session has been destroyed: the React Query cache still holds workspace/document data, and `PrivateRoute`'s `YorkieProvider` (PrivateRoute.tsx:23-28) keeps syncing with a previously minted Yorkie webhook token until it expires. Nothing clears the query cache or detaches the document when eviction is refused. Impact is bounded (the data is the same user's, and further API calls 401), but on a shared machine the authenticated view survives a logout the server already performed.

samples.summary: Releasing the redirect latch on a fixed 2 s timer can restart an in-flight eviction navigation, so session eviction may be repeatedly deferred on a slow connection
samples.evidence: Before this change the latch was permanent, so exactly one `window.location.href` assignment happened per tab. Now it is cleared after `REDIRECT_LATCH_MS = 2000` (auth.ts:57-61) with no check that a navigation is still in flight. If loading `/login` takes longer than 2 s — the slow/flaky-network case this whole feature targets — a later 401 from a background poller (e.g. the 5 s `refetchInterval` in `app/documents/page.tsx:24` and `workspaces/workspace-documents.tsx:34`) re-runs `logout()` and re-assigns `location.href`, aborting and restarting the eviction navigation. Repeated often enough, the user is never actually evicted client-side. I could not confirm browser-level restart semantics for an identical-URL assignment, hence low confidence.
searchedFor: read tests/api/auth.test.ts for a slow-navigation case

finding.summary: The 401 session-eviction redirect is refusable (and then permanently latched off) by the `beforeunload` guard this PR adds
finding.evidence: This delta states the invariant that "an app-issued redirect has to *be* a replace" so it cannot be refused (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-161), and fixes `PrivateRoute`/`PublicRoute` accordingly. The same invariant is violated by the other, non-router eviction path this PR newly made refusable. `fetchWithAuth` on a 401 calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` then `redirectTo("/login")` (api/auth.ts:153-160). `redirectTo` sets the module-level latch `isRedirecting = true` *before* assigning `window.location.href` (auth.ts:28-30). Earlier commits of this PR registered a `beforeunload` handler that calls `event.preventDefault()` whenever the document has unsent edits (components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103). A script-initiated `location.href` assignment fires `beforeunload`, so the browser shows the native "Leave site?" dialog; if the user picks "Cancel/Stay", the navigation to /login is aborted while `isRedirecting` stays `true` for the life of the tab. From then on every subsequent 401 in the session early-returns from `redirectTo` (auth.ts:28) and the thrown `AuthExpiredError` is deliberately swallowed by callers (e.g. app/templates/template-landing.tsx:116), so the expired session never evicts: the authenticated shell and the previously-fetched document content stay rendered indefinitely — a real exposure on a shared machine. Attacker/vector: any user (or an attacker who reaches an unattended tab) leaves an editor in the "not saved" state, waits for session expiry, and answers "Stay" once. I could not exercise a real browser to confirm the abort leaves the latch set, hence low confidence; the code path itself is traceable line by line. Fix would be to clear `isRedirecting` on a cancelled navigation (e.g. reset it in a `pagehide`/timeout) or to not latch before the assignment.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism — `isRedirecting` latched permanently after a refused `beforeunload`-guarded navigation, disabling all subsequent 401 evictions for the tab — is not present. `redirectTo` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:53-62) sets `isRedirecting = true` at :55 but immediately schedules a `setTimeout` at :57-60 that clears it after `REDIRECT_LATCH_MS = 2000` (:33). Grep shows `isRedirecting`/`redirectRelease` occur nowhere else in source (only api/auth.ts:25-60), so that timer is the sole and unconditional release path; it only fails to observably run when the navigation actually commits and tears the page down. If the user answers "Stay" to the handler at components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103, the page survives, the callback fires, and the next 401 in fetchWithAuth (api/auth.ts:184-192) re-attempts the redirect. This is precisely the fix the finding asks for, and it is documented as a deliberate inverse test in docs/design/sync-status.md:323-337. The reviewer's cited evidence lines (auth.ts:28-30) are comment text, not the latch. The only residual effect is a <=2s suppression window that self-clears — no persistent session-eviction bypass.
